Texas Business and Commerce Code Section 26.01 and Texas Property Code Section 5.021 are cited only for bounded Texas writing, signature, and conveyance-instrument propositions.

Energy Transfer Partners and Chalker Energy are used only as concrete examples showing why exact document language, separate obligations, definitive-agreement conditions, and execution conditions matter.
No source supports assigning an automatic legal status to a document label, deciding enforceability, interpreting a reader's document, determining title, or predicting a transaction result.
The article keeps the purchase agreement separate from the deed or other closing conveyance and preserves jurisdiction-specific professional-review boundaries.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Business and Commerce Code Section 26.01 (accessed 2026-09-15)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: Texas Business and Commerce Code Section 26.01 supplies the Texas writing-and-signature requirement for specified agreements, including a contract for the sale of real estate.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: It does not classify a reader's offer or LOI, decide enforceability, or provide individualized legal advice.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Property Code Section 5.021 (accessed 2026-09-15)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: Texas Property Code Section 5.021 supplies the separate written, subscribed, and delivered instrument rule for a Texas estate conveyance.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: It does not prove that an agreement is the closing conveyance or determine title, validity, or legal effect.

sources_inspected.label: Supreme Court of Texas, Energy Transfer Partners v. Enterprise Products Partners, No. 17-0862 (2020)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: Energy Transfer Partners v. Enterprise Products Partners supplies a concrete Texas example of nonbinding term-sheet language, separately stated obligations, and a definitive-agreement condition.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: It is an example of why exact language and stated conditions must be preserved, not a template or a decision about a reader's document.

sources_inspected.label: Supreme Court of Texas, Chalker Energy Partners III v. Le Norman Operating, No. 18-0352 (2020)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: Chalker Energy Partners III v. Le Norman Operating supplies a Texas example involving a definitive-agreement and execution condition in an asset-sale negotiation.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: It does not establish that every offer, LOI, email, or purchase agreement is binding or nonbinding.
